Title: On linear complementary pairs of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields
Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes and linear complementary pairs (LCP) of codes have been proposed for new applications as countermeasures against side-channel attacks (SCA) and fault injection attacks (FIA) in the context of direct sum masking (DSM). The countermeasure against FIA may lead to a vulnerability for SCA when the whole algorithm needs to be masked (in environments like smart cards). This led to a variant of the LCD and LCP problems, where several results have been obtained intensively for LCD codes, but only partial results have been derived for LCP codes. Given the gap between the thin results and their particular importance, this paper aims to reduce this by further studying the LCP of codes in special code families and, precisely, the characterisation and construction mechanism of LCP codes of algebraic geometry codes over finite fields. Notably, we propose constructing explicit LCP of codes from elliptic curves. Besides, we also study the security parameters of the derived LCP of codes $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{D})$ (notably for cyclic codes), which are given by the minimum distances $d(\mathcal{C})$ and $d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)$. Further, we show that for LCP algebraic geometry codes $(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})$, the dual code $\mathcal{C}^\perp$ is equivalent to $\mathcal{D}$ under some specific conditions we exhibit. Finally, we investigate whether MDS LCP of algebraic geometry codes exist (MDS codes are among the most important in coding theory due to their theoretical significance and practical interests). Construction schemes for obtaining LCD codes from any algebraic curve were given in 2018 by Mesnager, Tang and Qi in [``Complementary dual algebraic geometry codes", IEEE Trans. Inform Theory, vol. 64(4), 2390--3297, 2018]. To our knowledge, it is the first time LCP of algebraic geometry codes has been studied.

gold.abstract: Due to their widespread applications, linear complementary pairs (LCPs) have attracted much attention in recent years. In this paper, we determine explicit construction of non-special divisors of degree $g$ and $g-1$ on Kummer extensions with specific properties. In addition, we present several methods for constructing LCPs of algebraic geometry codes (AG Codes) via Kummer extensions. These results are applied in constructing explicit LCPs of AG Codes from subcovers of the BM curve, elliptic function fields, hyperelliptic function fields and other function fields. It is important to mention that we construct several families LCPs of MDS AG Codes from elliptic function fields and we obtain some linear complementary dual (LCD) codes from certain maximal elliptic function fields and hyperelliptic function fields.

--- Researcher B ---
SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper B constructs explicit linear complementary pairs (LCP) of algebraic geometry (AG) codes from elliptic curves over finite fields; derives conditions for \(C^\perp\) to be equivalent to \(D\); studies security parameter \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\); asks whether MDS LCP AG codes exist.
- Paper C characterizes LCP constacyclic and quasi-cyclic codes; shows for constacyclic pairs the dual of one code is equivalent to the other, simplifying the security parameter to one distance; reports binary examples with better parameters than known LCD codes.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
We hypothesize that AG codes built on curves with a cyclic automorphism group can be realized as constacyclic or quasi-cyclic codes. This would let Paper C’s algebraic LCP characterizations select divisor pairs within Paper B’s elliptic-curve AG constructions. The link is operational: a cyclic automorphism acting on function-field divisors induces a constacyclic shift on codewords, making Paper C’s criteria applicable to Paper B’s curve-based codes.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
Choose elliptic curves over \(\mathbb{F}_q\) with an order-\(n\) automorphism fixing a rational point. Construct AG evaluation/residue codes from automorphism-invariant disjoint divisor supports. Verify their constacyclic/quasi-cyclic representation explicitly. Apply Paper C’s LCP conditions to enumerate divisor pairs yielding LCP. Estimate \(d(C)\) via the Goppa bound and \(d(D^\perp)\) via dual AG parameters; compare \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\) with Paper C’s binary table and known LCD examples. Validate small cases in Sage/Magma. Missing cross-paper knowledge: neither source states that automorphism-invariant AG codes from elliptic curves inherit constacyclic/quasi-cyclic structure; this must be proven first, and Paper C’s binary tables cannot be assumed to transfer to AG codes until recomputed.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
This project connects elliptic-curve AG code constructions with constacyclic LCP characterizations. By representing automorphism-invariant AG codes as constacyclic/quasi-cyclic codes, we apply known algebraic LCP conditions to search for AG LCPs with improved minimum distances and dual-equivalence guarantees, potentially yielding better binary security parameters than known LCD codes.

FINAL IDEA: Use cyclic automorphisms of elliptic curves to represent algebraic geometry codes as constacyclic/quasi-cyclic codes, then apply constacyclic LCP characterizations to construct AG LCPs with provably improved minimum-distance security parameters.

--- Researcher C ---
SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS:
- Paper-b constructs linear complementary pairs (LCP) of algebraic geometry (AG) codes over finite fields, including explicit LCP codes from elliptic curves; it gives conditions under which \(C^\perp\) is equivalent to \(D\), and studies MDS LCP AG codes.
- Paper-c characterizes LCP codes within constacyclic and quasicyclic families, extends the Yang–Massey LCD characterization, and shows for constacyclic LCP that \(D^\perp\) is equivalent to \(C\), so security parameter \(\min(d(C),d(D^\perp))\) reduces to one minimum distance; it also gives binary double-circulant LCP codes and a programming bound.

INTEGRATION MECHANISM:
Use automorphism-induced quasicyclic structure as the operational bridge. Paper-b provides elliptic-curve AG LCP constructions; paper-c provides quasicyclic/constacyclic characterizations that collapse the security parameter and give parameter bounds. The proposed mechanism is that if an elliptic-curve AG LCP pair is invariant under a finite cyclic curve automorphism, it acquires a quasicyclic representation, making paper-c’s equivalence and bound results applicable. This connection is not established in either source.

RESEARCH DESIGN:
1. Construct elliptic-curve AG LCP pairs \((\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\) using paper-b’s divisor-based method over \(\mathbb{F}_q\), then impose a cyclic automorphism of order \(r\) on the curve and evaluate at orbits.
2. Test whether resulting \(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D}\) are quasicyclic of index \(r\) and whether paper-c’s constacyclic dual-equivalence condition holds.
3. Measure \(d(\mathcal{C})\) and \(d(\mathcal{D}^\perp)\) via Sage/Magma; compare \(\min(d(\mathcal{C}),d(\mathcal{D}^\perp))\) to paper-c’s programming bound for binary quasicyclic LCP codes.
4. Validate improvement: seek binary quasicyclic LCP parameters exceeding known LCD parameters from paper-c.

Missing cross-paper knowledge: no theorem linking AG-code automorphisms to quasicyclic LCP equivalence currently exists and must be derived.

WORKING ABSTRACT:
This project asks whether elliptic-curve algebraic geometry LCP codes can be realized as quasicyclic LCP codes, thereby inheriting the simplified security parameter and programming-bound guarantees available for constacyclic and quasicyclic families. We construct automorphism-invariant AG LCP pairs and test whether their induced quasicyclic structure satisfies the dual-equivalence criterion, potentially yielding binary LCP codes with better parameters than known LCD codes.

FINAL IDEA: Automorphism-invariant elliptic-curve AG LCP constructions are tested as quasicyclic LCP codes to collapse the security parameter and beat known LCD parameter bounds.
